    Interval restriction as object deletion #

    Nonnegative degrees prevent a nonzero factorization between interval objects from leaving the interval. Thus the finite interval category agrees with the object-deletion quotient, allowing use of the proved extension-by-zero module equivalence. This uses degree monotonicity, not a covering or averaging theorem.
